title: Set the starting id at init
lead: A project that continues numbering from an earlier tracker has to know that `add --id` advances the counter. `init` can't start the counter where it should be.
findings_note: agents-repo request R9: init cannot start the counter at S21; add --id works as a workaround
boundary: **Not in this slice:** an init option for the prefix or width (S145's territory); moving the counter on a project that already has items.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Request R9 from the squalor-xyz/agents orchestrator. Their old tree ends at S20, and new work should start at S21.

The counter is `Index.next_id` (`model.py:314`), written by `init` as `model.Index(id_prefix=..., id_width=...)` with the default 1 (`cli.py:313-336`). `init` takes only `--force` (`cli.py:1649-1650`).

The working workaround: `add "..." --id S21`. `ids.allocate` then raises `next_id` to 22 (`ids.py:68-89`), and later adds continue from there. It works, but only if you know `allocate` does that.

This depends on S145, which changes how `ids.parse_id` matches the prefix (case-insensitively) and touches the same `ids.py` code. Validating the starting id should use the rule S145 settles on.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `init` with a starting id of S21, then `add "x"`, allocates S21. The next add allocates S22.
2. A starting id with another prefix, or one that isn't valid under the configured width rules, exits 2 with code `bad_id` and writes nothing.
3. On an existing project with items, `init --force` with a starting id refuses (the counter would step back or skip over live ids), with a message pointing at `add --id`.
4. `init --force` with a starting id over an index with no items sets the counter.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Add the option to `init`. Validate the value with `ids.require_valid` and `ids.parse_id` against the configured prefix, then construct the new `Index` with `next_id` set to the parsed number. When an index already exists, only allow it if that index has no items. Mention it beside the one-way-door note in `docs/getting-started.md` (lines 114-118).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check` and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the re-rendered roadmap and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.
